short_description: A kneeling side stretch that opens the hips, inner thighs and lateral torso.
how_to: Kneel with your knees hip-width apart.
Extend your right leg straight out to the side.
Raise your left arm overhead and lean toward the right.
Hold for several breaths, then switch sides.
correct: Keep your hips stacked and square.
Reach long through your top arm.
Keep your extended leg foot flat on the floor.

short_description: A seated rolling movement that mobilises the entire spine and massages the back muscles.
how_to: Sit on the floor with your knees bent and feet flat.
Wrap your arms around your shins.
Tuck your chin and round your spine.
Roll back smoothly onto your upper back, then roll back up to sitting.
correct: Control the movement in both directions.
mistakes: Don't use momentum to jerk yourself up.
Don't land flat on your back.

short_description: A prone hip and spine rotation that stretches the hip flexors and strengthens the lower back.
how_to: Lie face down with your arms extended to the sides.
Bend your right knee and swing your right foot across toward your left hand.
Pause at the end range, then return.
Repeat on the other side.
correct: Keep your shoulders pressed into the floor.
mistakes: Don't force the foot further than your range allows.

short_description: A gentle floor movement that targets the lower spine, relieving stiffness and improving lumbar mobility.
how_to: Start on hands and knees with your wrists under your shoulders.
Inhale and let your lower back drop toward the floor.
Exhale and draw your lower belly up to round the lumbar spine.
Move slowly between the two positions.
correct: Keep your hips over your knees.
Focus the movement on your lower back.

short_description: A hands-and-knees movement that mobilises the mid-back, improving thoracic extension and flexion.
how_to: Start on all fours with a neutral spine.
Inhale and arch through your upper back, lifting your chest.
Exhale and round through your mid-back, drawing your shoulder blades apart.
Repeat in a slow, controlled rhythm.
correct: Focus the movement between your shoulder blades.
mistakes: Don't let your lower back do all the work.

short_description: A wide-leg forward fold that lengthens the hamstrings and inner thighs.
how_to: Set your feet wide apart.
Keep your back straight and hinge from your hips.
Reach your hands toward the floor.
Hold where you feel a gentle stretch.
correct: Keep a soft bend in your knees.

short_description: A seated forward stretch with small pulses that mobilises the spine and lengthens the hamstrings.
how_to: Sit tall with your legs straight in front of you.
Reach both arms forward at shoulder height.
Hinge from your hips and reach toward your feet.
Pulse gently forward a few inches without bouncing hard.
correct: Keep your back as straight as possible.
Hinge from your hips, not your waist.
Keep a soft bend in your knees.
mistakes: Don't round your upper back aggressively.

short_description: A gentle seated inner-thigh and hip stretch with a relaxed upright posture.
how_to: Sit on the floor and bring the soles of your feet together.
Let your knees fall out to the sides.
Hold your feet or ankles.
Sit tall and breathe steadily for the hold.
mistakes: Don't push down on your knees forcefully.

short_description: A seated hip-opener that stretches the inner thighs and groin with a deeper forward fold.
how_to: Sit on the floor and place the soles of your feet together.
Draw your heels close to your body.
Hinge forward from the hips over your feet.
Hold the position and breathe steadily.
correct: Keep your spine long as you fold.
Keep your shoulders away from your ears.
mistakes: Don't round your back to chase depth.

short_description: A kneeling stretch that gently lengthens the hamstring of the extended leg.
how_to: Kneel on one knee with your other leg extended in front.
Keep your front foot flat on the floor.
Sit tall and hinge slightly forward from the hips.
Hold where you feel a gentle pull behind the thigh.
correct: Keep a soft bend in your extended knee.

short_description: A kneeling hamstring stretch that builds on the easy version with a deeper hip hinge.
how_to: Kneel on one knee with the other leg extended straight in front.
Flex your front foot and point your toes up.
Hinge forward from the hips, keeping your back flat.
Hold at your comfortable end range and breathe.
correct: Hinge from the hips, not the waist.
mistakes: Don't lock your extended knee hard.

short_description: A deep lunge stretch that opens the hip flexors and groin while building lower-body stability.
how_to: Step one foot forward into a long lunge position.
Lower your back knee to the floor.
Keep your front shin vertical and your chest tall.
Hold the position and breathe steadily.
correct: Keep your knees over your toes.
Keep your heels down on your front foot.
mistakes: Don't let your knees cave inward.

short_description: A single-leg balance pose that strengthens the legs and improves focus and stability.
how_to: Stand tall and shift your weight onto one foot.
Place the sole of your other foot on your inner calf or thigh, avoiding the knee.
Bring your hands to prayer at your chest or raise them overhead.
Hold and breathe steadily, then switch sides.
correct: Keep your standing leg slightly soft, not locked.
Fix your gaze on a still point ahead.
mistakes: Don't press your foot against your knee joint.

short_description: A supine relaxation pose that allows the body and nervous system to rest fully.
how_to: Lie flat on your back with your legs slightly apart.
Let your arms rest at your sides, palms facing up.
Close your eyes and release all tension.
Breathe naturally and stay still for the hold.
correct: Relax your shoulders, jaw and hands.
Keep your body still and heavy.
Allow your feet to fall open.

short_description: A prone backbend that strengthens the back extensors and stretches the chest, shoulders and hip flexors.
how_to: Lie face down with your legs hip-width apart.
Bend your knees and reach back to hold your ankles.
Inhale and lift your chest and thighs off the floor.
Hold and breathe, then lower with control.
mistakes: Don't jerk your ankles to gain height.

short_description: An isometric push-up that builds chest, shoulder and core strength by holding the lowered position.
how_to: Start in a push-up position with your hands under your shoulders.
Lower halfway down until your elbows are bent.
Hold there with your body in a straight line.
Breathe steadily and keep your core tight.
correct: Keep your body straight from head to heels.
Keep your elbows close to your body.
mistakes: Don't raise your hips too high.
Don't flare your elbows out wide.

short_description: A kneeling plank that builds core and shoulder stability with reduced body-weight load.
how_to: Start on your hands and knees.
Walk your hands forward until your body forms a straight line from knees to shoulders.
Engage your core and hold the position.
Breathe steadily throughout.
correct: Keep your body in one line.
Keep your shoulders over your wrists.
mistakes: Don't let your lower back sag.
Don't lift your hips too high.

short_description: A deep lunge hip-opener that stretches the hip flexors, groin and inner thigh of the back leg.
how_to: Step one foot forward to the outside of your same-side hand.
Lower your back knee to the floor.
Keep both hands inside your front foot.
Hold and breathe, then switch sides.
correct: Keep your front knee over your ankle.
Keep your hips low and level.
mistakes: Don't let your front knee collapse inward.

short_description: A seated spinal twist that stretches the back muscles and improves thoracic rotation.
how_to: Sit with both legs extended.
Bend your right knee and place your right foot flat on the floor.
Twist your torso to the right and hook your left elbow outside your right knee.
Hold and breathe, then switch sides.
correct: Keep your spine tall as you twist.
mistakes: Don't collapse your spine as you rotate.
Don't force the twist beyond your range.

short_description: A seated balance that works the core and hip flexors by holding a V-shape with the torso and legs.
how_to: Sit on the floor with your knees bent.
Lean back slightly and lift your feet so your shins are parallel to the floor.
Extend your arms forward at shoulder height.
Hold the position and breathe steadily.
